extra.message: User input from request.args.get('name') is passed to the template and rendered with the | safe filter in unsafe_params.html line 6 ({{ name | safe }}), which disables Jinja2 auto-escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript via the 'name' GET parameter (e.g., ?name=<script>alert(1)</script>).

User input from request.cookies.get('name') or request.form.get('name') is passed to the template and rendered with the | safe filter in unsafe_cookies.html line 6 ({{ name | safe }}), which disables Jinja2 auto-escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript via the 'name' cookie or form parameter.

Stored user messages are rendered with the | safe filter (lines 29-31: message.from_user, message.message, message.date), which disables Jinja2 auto-escaping. Since the API POST endpoint (api/views.py:43) allows unauthenticated users to create messages, an attacker can store arbitrary JavaScript that will execute when an admin views the messages page.

The MessagesView.post() method lacks the @admin_required decorator, allowing any unauthenticated user to create messages via the API. Combined with the stored XSS vulnerability in the admin message template, this enables unauthenticated attackers to inject malicious scripts that execute in the admin's browser.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The 'next' parameter from request.args is used directly in redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL like /toggle_xss_protection/?next=https://evil.com to redirect users to a malicious site after they toggle XSS protection.

The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'Keep it secret, keep it safe'. This key is used for signing session cookies and CSRF tokens. An attacker who discovers this key can forge session cookies, potentially impersonating any user including the admin.

Passwords are stored as plaintext in the database (db.Column(db.String(200))) without any hashing. The User.__init__ method stores the raw password directly (self.password = password). This means anyone with database access can read all user passwords, and password hashing best practices (bcrypt, argon2) are completely absent.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Password verification is done by comparing plaintext strings (user.password == password). This confirms that passwords are stored and compared without any hashing, making them vulnerable if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The User.serialize property includes the plaintext password field ('password': self.password). This serialized data is exposed through the API endpoints (e.g., api/views.py UsersView.index), leaking user passwords to anyone with API access.

The username is rendered with the | safe filter ({{ g.user.username | safe }}), which disables Jinja2 auto-escaping. If a user with a malicious username (containing XSS payloads) exists, the script will execute on every page load for all users.

The hidden input value attribute is unquoted: value={{ g.path }}. The g.path comes from request.path which is user-controlled. Without quotes, certain characters in the path could break out of the attribute and inject additional HTML attributes or event handlers.

The form element uses unquoted attribute values: method={{ method }} and action={{ action }}. Without quotes, these attribute values could be broken out of if they contain spaces or special characters, potentially allowing attribute injection.
The textarea element uses unquoted attribute values: rows={{ rows }} and name={{ name }}. Without quotes, these attribute values could be broken out of, potentially allowing attribute injection.

The change_password, change_email, and send_feedback endpoints accept POST requests without any CSRF token validation. An attacker can craft a cross-origin form submission to change a victim's password, email, or send feedback on their behalf while the victim is authenticated.

DEBUG mode is enabled (app.config['DEBUG'] = True). In production, this exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which allows arbitrary code execution through the browser. An attacker who triggers an error can gain full control of the server.

The X-XSS-Protection header is explicitly set to 0 when XSS protection is toggled off, disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter. This removes a defense-in-depth mechanism that could help mitigate reflected XSS attacks.

When changing the password, the new password is stored directly in the database without hashing: User.query.filter_by(id=current_user.id).update({'password': new_password}). This is consistent with the plaintext password storage throughout the application.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The data-id attribute is unquoted: data-id={{ message.id }}. While message.id is currently an integer, this unquoted attribute pattern could be exploitable if the data source changes, and demonstrates the same unsafe attribute pattern used throughout the templates.
